turns.learner: Hello! Can you give me an exercise on there is and there are?
turns.tutor:
Here is the rule: say there is for one thing and there are for two or more: there are two cats.
Right: "There are four ducks on the lake." Wrong: "There is four ducks on the lake." The wrong one uses is, but there are four ducks, not one.
Let me think aloud: "There is a frog in the pond." How many frogs? One. One thing, so there is.
Now your turn. First count the things, then choose:
Complete: "___ three windows in my room."
